source: EMSCS Medical Oversight CQI Process, August 2025 revision (84 indicators); NJ EMS Clinical Practice Protocols v1 (8/21/2025). Methodology only — no PHI.

indicators.indicator: Does the chart adhere to the documentation standards policy and treatment protocols?
Does the HPI contain pertinent information regarding the present illness or injury, answering all the questions of why 911 was activated?
Does the activity log have a minimum of two full sets of vital signs, one of which is a manual BP, taken every 5 to 15 minutes based on acuity?
Does the activity log document completion of a primary, secondary or rapid assessment (the word Assessment appears)?
Does this patient have a pain level documented?
Does the final activity log entry name the receiving facility staff member who received report and transfer of care?
Does the chart identify securing the patient to all movement devices with a stated number of straps (3, 4 or 5)? All straps is not acceptable.
Are all medications and procedures documented by Add Action and not free typed in the comment field?
Was a deviation from protocol identified; if so, is there a special report filed identifying the deviation?
Were the appropriate signatures obtained? Required by federal law on all transports.
Were there any conflicting statements made in two separate places of the chart?
Was the patient transported to an appropriate facility?
Prior to cancellation of ALS, was a full patient assessment with vitals documented?
If ALS was cancelled, is the reason for cancellation documented?
If ALS was cancelled due to proximity, is the ETA or location of ALS at the time of cancellation documented?
Documentation of onset time with symptoms?
Documentation of prior interventions before 911 was called?
Initial assessment of pain type?
Documentation of duration of pain?
Documentation of the quality of pain?
Documentation of radiation of pain?
Documentation of whether palpation of the chest wall changes pain?
Documentation of gastric distress?
Appropriate oxygen therapy as indicated by perfusion (SpO2 below 92%)?
Chest pain treated per treatment protocol?
Did pain management interventions continue at regular intervals?
Documentation of patient taking aspirin or nitroglycerin, or why NTG or aspirin was not administered?
Illness or injury documented?
Date and time of injury documented?
Mechanism of injury, if applicable?
CPR initiated or continued?
Airway secured?
Illness or injury (MVI or additional injuries) documented?
Date and time of injury documented?
Mechanism of injury documented?
Initial assessment of pain and associated symptoms?
Appropriate oxygen therapy, if required?
Spinal immobilization maintained?
BP above 180 systolic or 100 diastolic, ALS requested if not dispatched?
Stroke scale documented?
Documentation of last time seen normal?
Was the head of the bed elevated 30 degrees?
Documentation of injury noted with burn?
Time of burn documented?
Burn exposure occurred in an enclosed or open space?
Exposure to toxic inhalation potential?
Percentage of body surface burned documented?
Degree of burns?
Airway assessment managed and secured?
Burn site wrapped in dry sterile sheets?
Estimated date of confinement (EDC)?
Gestational age documented?
Prior and prenatal history documented?
Documentation of gravida and para?
Documentation of onset of current labor?
Duration of uterine contractions?
Frequency of uterine contractions?
Documentation of distress, rales or pulmonary edema?
Is the level of respiratory effort documented (for example three word sentences, tripod position)?
SBP above 100 mmHg documented prior to CPAP?
Documentation that the patient was placed in Fowler's position?
Oxygen via CPAP documented by Add Action with PEEP in cm H2O, and SpO2 before and after?
All medications and procedures documented by Add Action identifying who performed them?
Were indications documented in the HPI or activity log prior to the medication?
Were route, dose, dose unit and response documented?
Was a clinical reassessment noted in the activity log after all medication administrations?
If ALS was not already dispatched or on scene, is there a documented request for ALS?
Were dosages appropriate and in compliance with the treatment protocols?
Specific documentation of COPD or asthma?
Documentation of pre therapy respiratory rate and SpO2?
Documentation of albuterol through Add Action?
If more than one, each administration more than 5 minutes apart?
Documentation of post therapy respiratory rate and SpO2?
Documentation of patient respiratory status post albuterol?
Was the refusal matrix completed in its entirety and properly signed?
Is each individual check box marked without a line through the entire section?
Does the chart document decision making capacity (answers appropriately, A&O x4)?
Does the activity log have a minimum of one full set of vital signs?
Are follow up instructions completed?
Does the chart document the patient was not under the influence of drugs or alcohol?
Was patient interest in help assessed, with ReachNJ documented in the HPI when appropriate?
Narcan leave behind documented by Add Action with route Not Administered, Left Behind?
Blood glucose documented by Add Action (Labs) identifying who performed it?
Wound care instructions provided and documented for the puncture site?
